body: Quick pass (UMA) @ 45373c9b: merges cleanly with upstream/main (v0.18.0), gate green at batch scope (geometry change: 9 steps incl. clippy), each pinning test fails on the old code, no goldens moved, body complete. Flagged ready for an independent review at the effort:high tier (generators/geometry).

<!-- pr-reviewer: 45373c9bda4bdf1dfc08db9ca98ba6f743a0ca70 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blockers found. This was a high-tier review: I read the logic adversarially and did not count the existing label or earlier review comments as evidence.

**What I built and ran.** I checked out head `45373c9b` (the branch was cut at v0.17.0) in its own worktree and trial-merged current `origin/main` (`a6bd69d8`). `material.rs` auto-merged and nothing conflicted. Every result below is on the merged tree.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry` (all binaries) | all passed, 0 failed |
| app face_holes / top_plane_noise / blind_floor / pocket_overhead / golden_cl / solid_law_goldens / area_picks | 3 / 2 / 7 / 2 / 25 / 1 / 5 passed |
| app operations / mill2d_b / mill2d_c | 117 (6 ignored) / 9 / 9 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

None of the touched tests builds a `VerifyContext` by hand, so the `model_excess` field added in #911 does not affect them.

**What I tried that held**
- **Can the weld join corners that are really distinct?** I wrote a local probe (not pushed, now deleted). It used your noisy-corner box, which forces the tolerant fallback, plus a second box across a slot:
  - Slot of 1.5 um: refused, `NonManifold`.
  - Slots of 2.5 um, 10 um and 1 mm: 2 loops, and the area is correct each time.
  - A separate 1.5 um wide sliver box on the same tolerant path: refused, `NonManifold`.
  In every case the result is either the right region or a named refusal. Corners within 2 um weld into degree-4 nodes, and the existing node check refuses those. Nothing is welded into a wrong but valid ring. Before this PR, the same meshes were refused as `Open`.
- **Where does the tolerance come from?** It is 2 um (Chebyshev) in the geo2d bridge's own 1 um grid (`slice_weld.rs:27`). It is absolute, not scaled to the part, and that is the right choice here: 1 um is the smallest step the region layer can represent, so no feature that can be machined lives under it. The tolerance only ever runs after the exact weld has returned `Open` (`slice.rs:96-99`). Every mesh that sliced before takes the byte-identical path, and golden_cl and solid_law_goldens are unchanged.
- **Buckets and casts.** `CELL = 4 >= WELD_TOL`, and the search covers the ±1 neighbour cells, so it reaches every point within tolerance. The key casts are `f64 -> i64` `as` (saturating; NaN goes to 0) after the slicer's horizon check, and the neighbour offsets use `saturating_add`. Lookups use `get`, and there is no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic` outside tests.
- **`section`'s empty retry.** The section is moved only 1 um down, and only after an empty answer. A plane that really misses the part still refuses, and the message now names the span. The `match` covers the `(Ok(empty), Err)` case the old code never retried.
- **`facet_shadow` as a pure union.** Wall facets of a vertical through hole project with zero area and are dropped, so through holes survive. Treating each triangle's shadow as material is the correct reading. The old nesting parity among triangles did not mean anything for this. This is only the fallback when `project` refuses.
- **Process.** `docs/decisions/241-cutouts-ops.md` is present (not RECOMMENDED.md), along with `Changelog:` and `Fixes #241`. The new module carries a provenance line, the tests live in their owning crates, and no snapshot PNGs, process files or dependencies changed.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. On the tolerant path, a mesh that is truly open and also has a sub-2 um feature now refuses as `NonManifold` instead of `Open`. It is still refused, but the message points at a different cause.
2. On a fallback-only mesh that is really open, `project` now slices each of its samples twice (exact, then tolerant). That is a cost, not a correctness issue.
3. `slice.rs` stays over the 400-line limit (466, down 2 lines).
4. Not exercised: the user's `cutouts.camproj` (not in the tree), the GUI, and the release heavy lanes. I ran the suites listed above, not the full batch tier.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
